# Integration contract v1

> **Release copy.** Generated by the release script from the private integration contract. Passages outside this release's scope, the private compute gate and records of who decided what are removed, and amendment headings keep only their dates. Section numbers are unchanged, so some cross-references point to removed text. This file is also the tools' repository-root marker.

**Status: frozen when committed.** Do not edit this file. Changes go into `phase/tools/CONTRACT_AMENDMENT_<n>.md`, one
file per amendment. Each amendment names the section it replaces and its reason. Amendment 1 (from P1f) is folded in
below as §5.4 because it arrived before the freeze. It is marked there.

Owner: integrator (`<branch>`). Integration branch: `integration`. Every `<branch>-*` branch writes and reads
exactly what is below. The fixture (§6) and `phase/tools/test_fixture.py` check a branch against the contract.

Plain-language summary:
- Everything is in scan voxels.
- Each patch carries an integer wrap number from our reference-free solve.
- A "switch" is a joined pair of patches that X6 would call adjacent-wrap. Our frozen reference-free classifier scores
  switch risk and flags pairs above its blind threshold.
- Outputs are one report, one overlay volume, one per-vertex table, cleaned patches, a spiral-constraints file and a
  pipeline9 filter.
- Metrics come from `phase/tools/metrics.py` and nowhere else.

---

## 1. Frame

- **Coordinates are scan voxels of PHerc1667 volume `20231117161658`, level 0, 7.91 µm.** Source:
  `https://dl.ash2txt.org/full-scrolls/Scroll4/PHerc1667.volpkg/volumes_zarr/20231117161658.zarr`. Its `.zattrs`
  `multiscales.axes` are `z, y, x`. Level 0 is `uint16`, shape `(11174, 3340, 3440)`, uncompressed 128³ chunks,
  `dimension_separator "/"`.
- **Axis order is the scan's: `z, y, x`.** Every volume, every voxel index and every packed coordinate array written
  under this contract is ordered `(z, y, x)`.
  - CSV files use named columns (`z`, `y`, `x`), never positional triples.
  - Exception: tifxyz keeps its own format, i.e. separate `x.tif`, `y.tif` and `z.tif` holding voxel coordinates.
  - Existing committed inputs use `(x, y, z)` triples: `phase/x1/patches.csv` bbox and centroid columns,
    `phase/x6/x6b_points.npz` `PA`/`PB`, and `phase/data_small/fixture/*.npz` (which copies those conventions; see
    its README). Converting them is the reader's job.
- **Units.** Coordinates are voxels. Lengths are voxels, or µm where the field name ends in `_um`. Areas are mm² or cm²,
  as named. Conversion: 1 voxel = 7.91 µm. µm appear only in display and named fields; computation is in voxels.
- **Reference.** The June 2026 complete surface is `20260612121456-w011_…_flatboi_straightened_v4`, 7.91 µm tifxyz,
  CC BY-NC 4.0. It is used for scoring only. It is a machine-assisted reconstruction, not ground truth.

## 2. Wrap index

- **Definition.** An integer per patch (or per vertex, when a patch is split). **+1 means one sheet outward.**
- **Values.** Exactly those of Q3c's reference-free consensus solve:
  - Function: `phase/q3/q3c_deploy.py` `solve_consensus_labels(state, uniform_weight)` at
    `<branch>` 0f5aa76, now on `integration`.
  - Weights are uniform: every measurement (i) and (ii) term weighs 1.0, and so does every (iii) term
    (`uniform_weight`).
  - The axis is `phase/h1/refmesh.py` `build_axis`. It is the area-weighted mean of patch centroids (`n` points as
    weights) per 256-voxel z bin, smoothed with a 3-bin uniform filter. It uses no reference input.
  - Angle: `θ = atan2(y − a_y(z), x − a_x(z)) mod 2π`, with `θ0 = 0`, i.e. the +x direction
    (`refmesh.ang`, `TH0 = 0.0`).
  - Cut: a term whose two endpoints lie on opposite sides of θ0 gets `d + s·c`, where `c = refmesh.cross(θa, θb)` is
    in {−1, 0, +1} (`q3c_deploy.cut_adj`).
  - Handedness: `s ∈ {+1, −1}` is whichever gives the lower LP objective (`q3c_deploy.choose_handedness`). On slab 2
    this is s = +1 (objectives 1306 vs 1582), the same as the reference's own `S_REF`. The reference is not read.
  - Solver: exact LP, `phase/h1/our_solver.py` `lp_synchronise`.
- **Committed values.**
  - `phase/p1page/p1b_q3c_k.csv` (`patch, k_q3c, component, thN`) is written by `p1b_q3c_k.py` from that function.
  - `k_q3c` is the wrap index. `thN` is θ. The continuous turn is `t = k + θ/2π`.
- **Gauge.** The index is defined up to one additive constant **per component** (`component` column). Compare indices
  only within a component. Report agreement with the reference only after fitting that constant per component.
  - Measured on slab 2: `k_q3c − k_ref` = +26 for 4,920 of 6,100 reference-labelled patches and +25 for 1,007.
  - The +25 group is X7's documented one-sided slip (layers −24 and inward).
- **Sign check.** Measured on slab 2, t correlates +0.81 with radius from the axis. So +1 is outward.
- **New data** (another slab, the whole scroll) must run the same function with the same weights, axis and cut rules
  and report the chosen s and both objectives. Changing any of them needs an amendment.

## 3. Switch

- **Pair.** X6's definition applies (`phase/x6/X6_protocol.json` step 3; `phase/x6/truth.py`).
  - A pair is a non-coincident overlapping patch pair from the witness enumeration (`phase/x4/x4.py`).
  - Its truth is the majority over up to 10 evaluated point pairs (normal separation > 1 voxel, seed 6).
  - **Adjacent** means `| |du| − 2πr | ≤ 0.25 · 2πr`. **Same-wrap** means `|du| < 5 mm`. A pair is **unresolved** if
    either point's normal distance to the reference is more than 0.4 × the local spacing. Coincident pairs are
    excluded.
  - Use `x6b_pairs.csv` `truth` as committed; the X9 erratum's 7 labels are not re-issued (ledger X-61).
  - **A switch is an adjacent pair.**
- **Risk.** The probability from `phase/tools/risk_model/risk_model_v1.joblib`: the Q3c reference-free consensus X8
  model, frozen. Q3c itself committed no deployable model and no blind threshold, so v1 is a separately recorded
  version built only from Q3c's functions (`build_risk_model.py`).
  - Label: `round(k_b − k_a) ≠ 0` from §2's solve.
  - Model: `HistGradientBoostingClassifier(class_weight="balanced", random_state=8)`, trained on the 7,087 pairs Q3c
    used.
  - Features, in this order: `sep_um, median_count, agreement, n_testable, support_fraction, stevens_dist_vox, area_a,
    area_b, z_um`.
    - Their definitions are `phase/x8/build_dataset.py`'s. P11 confirmed that `sep_um` is the witness's own pair
      separation (`phase/x4/x4.py:149` → `switchwitness/core.py:201`) with no reference input.
    - `stevens_dist_vox` may be NaN (pairs pipeline9 did not align).
  - Reproduction check: nested CV plus matched precision 0.825 gives Q3c's committed reference-free recall exactly,
    0.8709 (`risk_model_v1.json` R1).
- **Flag.** `risk ≥ 0.3293271860685008`. This is the **blind threshold**: 4-fold patch-z out-of-fold probabilities,
  precision 0.85 against the model's own reference-free label. The reference is not read to choose it.
  - Scored against the reference as a check (not a claim): OOF precision 0.837, recall 0.840. Per-fold nested
    thresholds give 0.800 / 0.847.
  - The blind point therefore lands below the 0.85 precision it targets on its own labels. Quote it as measured.
- **Contact regime.** Pairs with `sep_um < 50` are the contact regime. Report them separately everywhere. The checker
  has no working measurement there: Q1 contact recall at precision 0.85 is 0.017, and prevalence is 1.9 %.

## 4. Files

A run over a region writes one directory `<out>/`. Every JSON file carries `"contract": "v1"`, the `git` head of the
producing branch, the region (`origin_zyx`, `shape_zyx`, voxels) and the input hashes (SHA-256).

### 4.1 `report.json`
```json
{
  "contract": "v1", "git": "<sha>", "branch": "<branch>-...",
  "region": {"origin_zyx": [z, y, x], "shape_zyx": [nz, ny, nx]},
  "inputs": {"<path or url>": "<sha256>"},
  "counts": {
    "patches": int, "patches_with_wrap_index": int, "wrap_components": int,
    "joins": int, "pairs_scored": int, "pairs_flagged": int, "pairs_flagged_contact": int,
    "pages": int, "wrong_turn_patches": int, "wrong_turn_points": int
  },
  "areas_cm2": {"patches_bbox": float, "pages": float, "flagged_suspect": float, "wrong_turn": float, "cleaned_kept": float},
  "metrics": {"<variant>": <metrics.py summary dicts, §5>},
  "clusters": [
    {"id": int, "kind": "suspect_join" | "wrong_turn",
     "n_pairs": int, "n_patches": int, "area_cm2": float,
     "centroid_zyx": [z, y, x], "bbox_zyx": [[z0, y0, x0], [z1, y1, x1]],
     "theta_deg": float, "wrap_index_range": [kmin, kmax],
     "patches": [int], "pairs": [[a, b]], "max_risk": float}
  ]
}
```
- **Clusters.** Flagged pairs, or wrong-turn patches, joined by single linkage when their evaluated points come within
  `50 µm` (6.32 voxels) of each other. Coordinates are voxels, `(z, y, x)`.

### 4.2 Overlay: `overlay.zarr`
- OME-Zarr (NGFF 0.4) on Zarr v2, `uint8`.
  - **0** none, **1** suspect join, **2** wrong-turn area. Where both apply, the higher value wins.
- Level 0 has the scan's voxel grid over the region, with 128³ chunks aligned to the scan's chunk grid (region origin
  a multiple of 128), and `dimension_separator "/"`.
  - The compressor is free.
  - `multiscales.axes` are `z, y, x` with `unit "micrometer"`. Each dataset has `scale` `[7.91·2^l]*3` and a
    `translation` equal to the region origin × 7.91.
  - Levels 1+ are 2× **max**-pooled, so flags survive downsampling.
- **Rasterisation.**
  - Value 1: every voxel within 3 voxels of any evaluated point (PA, PB and their midpoint) of a flagged pair.
  - Value 2: every voxel containing a tifxyz vertex of a wrong-turn point (§5.4 minority points), dilated by 1 voxel.

### 4.3 Per-vertex CSV: `vertices.csv`
- One row per valid tifxyz vertex of every patch in the region.
- Columns: `patch, row, col, z, y, x, wrap_index, theta, page, page_majority_n, n_ref, ref_ok, wrong_turn, suspect,
  max_risk`.
  - `n_ref` is §5.4's per-point reference winding in the page frame; empty if `ref_ok` = 0.
  - `wrong_turn = (ref_ok and n_ref != page_majority_n)`.
  - `suspect` is 1 if the vertex lies within 3 voxels of a flagged pair's evaluated point.
  - `max_risk` is the highest risk over pairs touching the patch.

### 4.4 Cleaned tifxyz: `cleaned/<page>/patch_<id>/{x,y,z}.tif, meta.json`
- Stevens' tifxyz layout: float32, `scale [0.25, 0.25]`.
- Removed cells are set to **−1** in all three tifs, the invalid sentinel.
- Cells are removed when they are wrong-turn vertices; a patch whose wrong-turn share exceeds 50 % is dropped
  entirely.
- `meta.json` keeps the original keys and adds `"contract": "v1", "source_sha256": {...}, "removed_cells": int`.
- Flagged joins are not in tifxyz. They are listed in `report.json` and in `pipeline9/removed_joins.csv`.

### 4.5 Spiral constraints: `spiral_constraints.json`
- Envelope (frozen):
  `{"contract": "v1", "git", "region", "frame": "scan voxels zyx, 7.91 um", "wrap_index_source": "§2", "format":
  "<name>", "format_doc": "phase/tools/SPIRAL_CONSTRAINTS.md", "constraints": [...]}`.
- **The record schema is SessE's.** SessE commits `phase/tools/SPIRAL_CONSTRAINTS.md` on its `<branch>-*` branch. From the
  merge that brings it in, it is part of this contract by reference. It may not redefine §1–§3.

### 4.6 pipeline9 filter: `pipeline9/`
- **Inputs:**
  - `rel.csv` as pipeline9's aligner writes it (P9 format, `phase/x5/rel.csv`: `patch_a, patch_b, flip, …` affine
    columns).
  - `badpatchscores_b.csv` (`patch2, patch1, maxDistance`) when available.
  - The pair risk table (`switch_risk.csv`: `patch_a, patch_b, risk, flagged`).
- **Outputs:**
  - `rel_filtered.csv`: the same format, rows of flagged joins removed, everything else byte-identical.
  - `removed_joins.csv`: `patch_a, patch_b, risk, sep_um, contact (0/1), reason`.
  - `badpatches_b.csv` if the filter also flags patches, in pipeline9's format (one id per line).
  - `filter.json`: counts, threshold, contract version.
- **README claim limit** (amendment 1, §5.4): the filter's README may claim only the per-point M2 gain, and only once
  P1g confirms it.

## 5. Metrics

Compute every metric with `phase/tools/metrics.py`. It is checked against ledger rows SessN8-04 and SessN4-01 by
`phase/tools/test_metrics.py`.

### 5.1 Pages
- Pages are union-find components of the kept joins with area ≥ 1 cm².
- Patch area is the xy bounding box (P1c), unless per-point area is stated.
- Joins come from `rel.csv` minus `phase/x10/flip1_pairs.csv`.

### 5.2 M1, M3 (two labellings, always both)
- **M1**: page area in pages with no cross-turn join, as a share of all page area.
- **M3**: cross-turn joins per cm² of page area.
- **Labellings:**
  - *Per-patch layer*: `|t_a − t_b| > 0.5`, with `t = k_ref + θ/2π` (`metrics.cross_per_patch_layer`).
  - *X6 pairs*: truth `adjacent`; unresolved joins and joins without an X6 row are excluded and counted
    (`metrics.cross_x6`).
- **Required note, wherever M1 is quoted:** every residual cross-turn join in every cleaned variant is a contact-regime
  join. The reference is inconsistent there (P1f: all 64 in (iii-rf), all 22 in (ii); median ≈ 23 µm). So **M1 cannot
  rank methods until those joins have human adjudication.**

### 5.3 Recall at precision; intervals
- **Threshold at precision p:** the lowest score whose descending-rank precision is ≥ p (`metrics.threshold_at_precision`).
- **Blocks:** 12 θ-sectors × 4 z-slabs.
  - z-slabs are equal quarters of the evaluated region's z-extent. The fixed 192-voxel slabs from z 4096 are the
    same thing on slab 2.
  - A pair's θ is the circular mean of its two patches' θ.
- **Bootstrap:** 1,000 draws of 48 blocks with replacement.
  - Page metrics weight patches, and a join carries its smaller-id patch's weight. Pair metrics weight pairs.
  - Calls stay fixed (evaluation-only).
  - The seed is recorded in the output.
- **Defect exclusion (P1f):** `metrics.defect_at` at each join's median-separation X6 point-pair midpoint, against the
  ×4-upsampled reference.
  - **Displaced**: no reference vertex within 60 µm.
  - **Duplicated**: reference sheets from columns more than 100 apart within 60 µm and within 25 µm of each other.
  - Reported as M1-excl and M3-excl, next to (never instead of) M1-X6 and M3-X6.

### 5.4 Amendment 1 (from P1f), folded in before freeze
- **Page purity headline = M2 computed per point** (`metrics.m2_point_records` / `summarize_m2_point`). It is the
  area-weighted fraction of each page's points on the page's majority reference turn.
  - Per point: `n = round(t_ref − (θ + off_P)/2π)`. Here `t_ref` is the reference's continuous turn at the nearest
    ×4-upsampled reference vertex within 60 µm, and `off_P` is the page-local 2π unwrap of patch P over the page's
    joins. That makes n the reference winding in the page's own frame, so a page crossing θ0 is not penalised.
  - Points with no reference within 60 µm are excluded and counted.
  - Each point is one tifxyz cell (4 × 4 voxels, 1.00 × 10⁻³ mm²).
  - P1c's per-patch M2 (`M2_patch`) stays in tables as a secondary column.
- **M1 is reported under both labellings** (§5.2) with the note above. M1 cannot rank methods pending human
  adjudication.
- **The pipeline9 filter's README may claim only the per-point M2 gain, once P1g confirms it.**

## 6. Fixture and tests
- **Fixture:** `phase/data_small/fixture/` (see its README): two 384³ crops of X3 slab 2 (A with CT, B at the θ0 cut,
  geometry only), their patches, X6 labels, joins, features, reference subset, and golden outputs from existing code.
  - On the fixture only, the page threshold is **0.1 cm²** (`page_min_mm2` in `golden/pages_metrics.json`), because
    real pages are larger than a 3 mm crop. Page code must take the threshold as a parameter.
  - Fixture risk flags are in-sample for the risk model. The fixture tests formats and reproduction, never
    performance.
- **Example:** `phase/tools/example_outputs.py DIR` writes a correct set of §4 outputs for region A from the golden
  values and passes the validator. It shows the formats; it is not a method.
- **Tests:**
  - `phase/tools/test_metrics.py`: ledger reproduction.
  - `phase/tools/test_fixture.py`: golden outputs, plus a format validator for §4 outputs
    (`python3 phase/tools/test_fixture.py --outputs <out>`).
- A `<branch>-*` branch is merged only if both tests pass on the merge result and its numbers are reproducible from
  committed data (`phase/writeup/MERGE_PROTOCOL.md`).

## Amendment 2 (2026-09-27)

§1–§6 above are unchanged. This amendment **replaces §4.5's delegation**.
The spiral-constraint record format is now fixed here, not in a separate `SPIRAL_CONSTRAINTS.md`. Sources are
SessE's quotations of `ScrollPrize/villa` `main` @ `f4570bf` (the format predates PR #1788 `a92521b`; PR #1784 `2b81ea5`
contains no winding format).

### A2.1 Files
- One VC3D point-collection JSON file per role, in `<out>/spiral/`:
  - `abs_winding.json`
  - `relative_windings.json`
  - `same_windings.json`
- The role is decided by the file name alone (`fit_session.py`, `PCL_ROLE_CONVENTIONS`: *"(PclRole.ABSOLUTE,
  "abs_winding.json"), (PclRole.RELATIVE, "relative_windings.json"), (PclRole.SAME_WINDING, "same_windings.json")"*).
  `metadata.winding_is_absolute` is ignored (`fit_spiral.py`: *"Absolute-winding status is determined solely by the
  source file … Any metadata key in another file is ignored."*).
- `<out>/spiral_constraints.json` (§4.5 envelope) stays as the manifest. `format` = `"vc_pointcollections_json v1"`,
  `format_doc` = `"phase/tools/CONTRACT.md Amendment 2"`, and `constraints` lists the role files written, each with
  its SHA-256 and counts.

### A2.2 Schema (`point_collection.py`, `load_point_collection`)
```json
{"vc_pointcollections_json_version": "1",
 "collections": {"<int id>": {"name": "str", "color": [r, g, b], "metadata": {},
   "points": {"<int id>": {"p": [x, y, z], "wind_a": 0.0, "creation_time": 0}}}}}
```
- **`p` = (x, y, z) in dataset voxels.** For us that is PHerc1667 `20231117161658`, 7.91 µm. This is a second named
  exception to §1's (z, y, x) rule, like tifxyz. villa reverses it internally (`_point_zyxs`: *"point.get('zyx',
  point['p'][::-1])"*).
- **`wind_a` = winding number** (turns). **A `wind_a` difference is a physical layer difference.**
  - `losses.py`: *"'winding_diff': p2['winding_annotation'] - p1['winding_annotation']"*.
  - Our §2 wrap index has +1 = one sheet outward, so it maps to `wind_a` with the same sign. **Villa handles its own
    θ = 0 seam** (*"expected -= _pcl_chain_seam_adjustments(...)"*). A producer therefore exports Δk with **our** §2
    cut term removed (Δ = k_b − k_a − s·cross(θa, θb)) and never adds a seam term of its own.
- Chain order: with the default `pcl_rel_winding_adjacent_patches_only = True`, only consecutive points pair
  (*"candidates = list(zip(patch_ids, patch_ids[1:]))"*). So we write one 2-point collection per constrained patch
  pair, named `between_patches__<a>__<b>`.
- A point is used only if a patch surface lies within `pcl_link_distance_tolerance` = 2.5 voxels (README #1788).
  Unattached points are silently dropped. On a **name mismatch** villa silently snaps to the largest-area patch within
  2.5 voxels (`_resolve_between_patches_targets`).
- Mixed annotations: unannotated points are stripped with a warning (`normalise_pcl_winding_annotations`).

### A2.3 Soft only
- **All winding constraints are soft.** There is **one global L1 weight of 5.0 per role**: *"self.loss_weight_rel_winding
  = 5.0 / self.loss_weight_abs_winding = 5.0"* (`config.py`); losses are *"_masked_all_pairs_l1(..., expected)"*.
- **There is no hard flag and no per-point or per-collection weight.** A producer must not claim otherwise.
- Risk may enter only as sampling frequency: replicated collections, or per-file groups
  (`pcl_sampling_group_weight`: *"When the dict is in use every group must have an explicit key"*). That is an
  expectation-level weight, not a loss weight, and must be labelled so.
- Oracle or reference-derived files are labelled `oracle` and never deployed.

### A2.4 Compute
- **The fitter is GPU-only.** `fit_spiral.py` `run()` calls `self.check_cuda_ready()` unconditionally before loading
  (probe `torch.empty(1, device='cuda')`; `PatchAtlas(..., device='cuda')`; `storage_backend='sparse_cuda'`). Inputs
  load on CPU; fits do not.
- The three prerequisites (tifxyz folders named by patch id, `umbilicus.json`, outward sense) are tracked in
  `phase/writeup/OPEN_ITEMS.md`.

## Amendment 3 (2026-09-27)

It replaces the terms "risk" in §3–§4 and the record rules of Amendment 2 where they
conflict. The file formats (column names) are unchanged.

### A3.1 Two terms, not one "risk"
- **Switch score** = risk model v1's probability (§3), flagged at the committed blind threshold 0.3293271860685008.
  - It drives overlay value 1 (suspect join) and the pipeline9 filter.
  - The existing names `risk`, `max_risk` and `switch_risk.csv` are kept for format stability. They **mean switch
    score.**
- **Error score** = the probability that our wrap index is wrong at a join. **None exists.**
  - Risk model v1 is trained on `round(k_b − k_a) ≠ 0` from the Q3c solve itself. It learns to agree with the index.
  - Against actual index errors it scores AUC 0.506 (SessE-2 (a), 453 disagreeing edges vs matched agreeing ones).
  - **It must not be described anywhere as an error, doubt or confidence estimate.**
- SessA's README and any viewer text: **"flags mark where the index changes, not where it is doubtful."**

### A3.2 Spiral constraints: the shipped export (final for this phase)
- **The export is uncut, uniform and per-patch.**
  - `wind_a` = the patch's §2 wrap index `k_q3c` at every exported point.
  - One collection is written per X6 evaluated point pair (`phase/sc/convert.py` `write_points`).
  - Weights are uniform. There is **no filter variant**: no suspect-join cut, no contact abstention, no
    risk-derived replication.
  - Files, as scored in SessE-3 (`phase/sc/results/sc3_ab_points.json` `k_q3c.export`):
    - `spiral/same_windings.json`: 141,449 point pairs, sha256 `0009f911…1c83`.
    - `spiral/relative_windings.json`: 4,808 point pairs, sha256 `100f8db9…1123`.
  - Why: the suspect cut deleted switch constraints that were 92 % correct (per-point hard accuracy 0.763 uncut vs
    0.518 cut). Cuts are for pages, not constraints.
- **Per-vertex `wind_a`, requested at the SessE-2 stage, is withdrawn for this phase** by the SessE-3 ship decision.
  - No reference-free intra-patch winding exists yet.
  - The route past the per-patch ceiling is SessA's open item: a per-vertex wrap index from the field
    (`phase/writeup/OPEN_ITEMS.md`).
- **Seam convention** (SessE-2): cut θ0 = +x, `θ = atan2(y − a_y, x − a_x)`.
  - `c = +1` when the short path from a to b crosses θ0 counter-clockwise (θ rising through 2π → 0).
  - Export `Δ = k_b − k_a − c` (Amendment 2's `s·cross` with s = +1). villa adds back its own θ = 0 crossings.
- **Outward sense.** villa's "CW" is in image coordinates (y down). Handedness +1 means k increases with θ; the LP
  objective and X6's `S_REF` both give it (SessE-2 (f)). So `spiral_outward_sense = "CW"`. **No human step.**

## Amendment 4 (2026-09-27)

**§4.2 is replaced**; values 0/1/2 and the rasterisation rules stay as in §4.2.

### A4.1 Overlay: full-frame sparse OME-Zarr
- **Why.** VC3D silently draws nothing for a non-zero OME translation
  (`core/src/render/ZarrChunkFetcher.cpp:757`, "OME coordinate translations must be finite and zero"). Evidence:
  SessD's `evidence/silent_misplacement_preguard.png`. SessD's zero-offset copy is byte-exact against the golden after a
  chunk rename, so this costs nothing.
- **On-disk format: Zarr v2** (`.zgroup`, `.zarray`, `.zattrs`), independent of the Python zarr library version.
  - SessD's in-app run drew a v2 array with blosc-lz4.
  - SessD is to confirm the version VC3D reads (expected v2); the contract fixes v2 either way.
- `<out>/overlay.zarr` holds one array per scan level l = 0..5:
  - **shape = the scan's level shape**: (11174, 3340, 3440), (5587, 1670, 1720), (2794, 835, 860), (1397, 418, 430),
    (699, 209, 215), (350, 105, 108);
  - chunks 128³, `dimension_separator "/"`, `uint8`, `fill_value 0`;
  - compressor blosc (`lz4`, clevel 5, shuffle 1), the configuration VC3D was seen to draw.
- **No translation**: each dataset has only `scale [7.91·2^l]*3` (µm); a translation, if present, must be exactly 0.
  Axes are z, y, x.
- **Only chunks inside the region are written.**
  - Region = the segment's bbox plus the halo (`--halo-um`, default 80), snapped outward to the chunk grid of each
    level.
  - No stored chunk may lie outside it. All-zero chunks inside it may be omitted, since the fill is 0.
  - Level l is the 2× max-pool of level l−1 in absolute scan coordinates.
- `report.json` `region` = the level-0 snapped region (`origin_zyx` a multiple of 128).
- A VC3D `meta.json` sits beside `.zgroup`: `type "vol"`, `uuid`, `name`, `format "zarr"`, `width/height/slices` =
  scan x/y/z, `voxelsize 7.91`.
- **Roles.** SessA writes this natively. SessD's placement guard stays as a safety check. `overlay_vc3d.zarr` is no longer
  needed.
- **Reference implementation:** `phase/tools/contract_io.py` `write_overlay_fullframe`, used by
  `example_outputs.py`.

### A4.2 Command line (SessA and SessD both bind to it)
```
vc_sheet_check --segment <tifxyz dir | .obj> --volume <ome-zarr root> --out <dir> [--halo-um 80] [--threshold <switch-score threshold, default 0.3293271860685008>]
```
- **Exit codes:** 0 success; 2 invalid input; 3 internal error.
- **Output paths:** `<out>/report.json`, `<out>/overlay.zarr` and `<out>/vertices.csv`, always at those paths.
- **`report.json` status:** `"status": "ok"` on exit 0. On exit 2 or 3 the tool still writes `<out>/report.json`
  with `"status": "error"` and `"error": "<message>"` if it can, and no overlay.
- Consumers treat any non-zero exit as failure whatever files exist.

### A4.3 Cluster coordinates are zyx
- `report.json` `centroid_zyx` and `bbox_zyx` are stored in scan axis order (z, y, x), as §1 requires.
- Any consumer converting to (x, y, z) for a viewer does so explicitly and tests it. SessD's swap test is the model:
  the focus POI must equal `centroid_zyx` reversed.

### A4.4 Fixture v1.1 (additive; v1 files unchanged)
- `golden/report.json`: `example_outputs.py`'s region-A report with §4.1 clusters (31 suspect-join, 21 wrong-turn).
- `golden/expected_cross_turn_clusters.json`: the X6-confirmed cross-turn joins in region A (30 joins, 13 clusters,
  by §4.1's rule). Their coordinates are listed in the fixture README.
- **Rule:** a detector claim is merged only if it is tested against these expected clusters on the fixture. The
  14:00 merge blocks any detector claim without that test.

### A4.5 Library pins
- `zarr==2.18.7` in `phase/requirements.txt` and `phase/tools/requirements.txt`, which also pins the other
  versions the tools were run with.
- `example_outputs.py`, `contract_io.py` and the fixture tests run under the pin.

It supersedes the conflicting parts of Amendment 4.

### A5.1 Overlay: one variant only (adopts SessA's `AMENDMENT_PROPOSAL_overlay.md`)
- **The sole overlay is `<out>/overlay.zarr` in the full scan frame**, as specified in Amendment 4 §A4.1: translation
  0, scan chunking, only region chunks stored, levels 0–5 max-pooled, VC3D `meta.json`.
- **The cropped, translated variant is dropped entirely**, and so is a separate `overlay_vc3d.zarr`. Consumers who

    is attached and reported active but is not drawn at its position.
  - villa `main` @ f4570bf, `volume-cartographer/core/src/render/ZarrChunkFetcher.cpp`:
    - lines **976–980**: `openLocalZarrPyramid` opens levels by their path keys only, so a local translation is
      ignored;
    - line **755**: the strict remote parser throws "OME coordinate translations must be finite and zero".
    - Amendment 4 cited line 757 from SessD; integrator read the file at f4570bf, and **755** is the throw.

### A5.2 Two separate parameters: halo and field period
- **Halo = 80 µm** (`--halo-um`, default 80): the spatial margin of the field and the region around the mesh bbox. It
  is not a period.
- **Field period (log-Gabor band-pass centre) = 118.66950981993529 µm**, the training value
  (`phase/x3/results/slab2/field.json` `period_um`), at which the switch score's features were computed.

  (`phase/tools/vc_sheet_check/validation/SessA-2_PROTOCOL.md`).
- SessA's 80 µm field period was a misreading of the brief's 80 µm, which meant the halo. Outputs made at 80 µm must say
  so and are not contract outputs.

### A5.3 Axis for orientation
- The field and every θ are oriented about **the scroll axis**, never about a crop's own centre.
  - **Region mode (patches present):** §2's axis (`refmesh.build_axis` on the region's patch set).
  - **Segment mode (no patches):** a supplied axis file, required.
    - The scan's umbilicus in villa's `umbilicus.json` format (SessE's deliverable, OPEN_ITEMS G-b), or a CSV with
      columns `z,y,x` (scan voxels), linearly interpolated in z.
    - For PHerc1667 slab 2: `phase/tools/axis/pherc1667_x3slab2_axis.csv` (§2's axis, z 3968–4992, written by
      `make_axis_csv.py`).
    - Its path and sha256 go in `report.json` `inputs`.
    - A segment whose z range leaves the file's range by more than 256 voxels is invalid input: exit 2.
    - **No axis file means exit 2.**
- **Crop-centre orientation is forbidden.** SessA found that S1b's crop-centre orientation gave recomputed crossing
  counts with correlation **−0.92** against the committed features. With the contract axis it is **+0.93**, with

### A5.4 "Join", one definition
- **A join is an unordered patch pair that appears in `rel.csv` at least once, excluding pairs whose only rows have
  flip = 1** (`phase/x10/flip1_pairs.csv`). Duplicate rows and both directions count once.
- `report.json` `counts.joins` = the joins among the region's patches, before any cut.
- Variant join sets are this set filtered by the variant's rules.
- This is P1c's common join set (10,240 on slab 2). **P1e's hybrid row (8,007 joins) was counted this way:** 10,240
  → (iii-rf) 9,825 → pipeline9 deletions 8,007 → pruning 0. SessA counts it the same way.

## Amendment 6 (2026-09-27). Adds to §5 (metrics)

### A6.1 On-ridge tests need a calibrated per-product offset
- **Finding (post hoc diagnostic, SessE-4):** segmentation points trace a papyrus **face** about 20–24 µm inside the
  CT density ridge, not the ridge itself.
  - Mean CT profile along the outward normal peaks at **+3.0 voxels** on undisputed control hits (23.7 µm) and
    **+2.5 voxels** on core anchors (19.8 µm): `phase/sc/results/sc4_a_diag_profile.json`.
  - SessA's mesh-on-papyrus check found **+15.82 µm** on a Scroll 4 mesh and **−15.82 µm** on a Scroll 1 mesh
    (`<branch>` `validation/results/*/alignment_profile.json`). That is one sampling step at 15.82 µm; the sign
    follows each mesh's normal orientation.
- **Rule.** Any test that asks whether a face-tracing product (patches, segments, meshes, surface predictions, their
  medials) lies "on a CT ridge" must first apply a per-product signed offset along the normal, calibrated as follows:
  - measured on **control data only**, which is undisputed and disjoint from the test set;
  - pre-registered and frozen before any test point is read;
  - reported with its sign convention, its spread (IQR) and a fold-to-fold stability check.
  - The calibrated hit rate is primary. The zero-offset rate is reported beside it for the record.
- **What this re-reads:**
  - SessE-2/SessE-3 core rays: now void (A6.2).
  - SessA's alignment check: it shows the meshes lie on papyrus, not on the ridge.
  - SessC's step (2): P-A 52.4 % on-ridge and the exploratory 055 79.5 % used a ±15 µm window with no calibrated
    offset. Neither is a placement-accuracy number until re-scored under this rule (ledger item-27, item-30, item-40).

### A6.2 CT-ray adjudication needs a passing control gate
- A ray method may adjudicate a disputed index only after it passes a pre-registered sanity gate on undisputed
  control rays, with the A6.1 offset applied.
- SessE-4's gate failed: 18 % of control hits on-ridge at ±1 voxel against a 7 % null, and 7 % of rays valid.
  **Every CT-ray adjudication of the core block is void:** SessE-2 (c)(i) short rays, SessE-3 (d) long rays, and both
  "neither" rays.
- **The shipped spiral export (Amendment 3 §A3.2) is unaffected.** It reads no CT; villa links points to the patch
  surface, not to a CT ridge.

## Amendment 7 (2026-09-27)

It supersedes the conflicting parts of Amendments 5 and 6.

### A7.1 Halo = 380 µm (reverses A5.2's 80 µm)
- **`--halo-um` default 380** (48 L0 voxels). The 80 µm in the brief was unmotivated.
  - A halo under one sheet spacing cannot contain the neighbouring wrap that a jump lands on.
  - 380 µm is SessA's original 48-voxel halo.
- The field period stays **118.66950981993529 µm** (A5.2).
- SessA-2's post hoc arm at 118.67 µm and 380 µm gave the highest coverage of its arms (16.4 %). That is recorded, not
  used as a justification.

### A7.2 §4.1 cluster fields, defined (fixture v1.3, reconciled with SessA)
- **Evaluated points** of a flagged pair = PA, PB and their midpoint, as §4.2 already said. Clustering and
  rasterisation use the same set.
- **Suspect-join `area_cm2`** = the number of vertices flagged `suspect` in the cluster's patches × one tifxyz cell,
  (4 × 7.91 µm)².
- **Wrong-turn `area_cm2`** = the cluster's wrong-turn vertices × one cell.
- **`max_risk`** = the maximum switch score over the cluster's pairs. It is **null for wrong-turn clusters**, which
  have no pairs.
- `theta_deg` is compared to 0.01°. Cluster `id` order is free.
- **Report `areas_cm2`:**
  - `patches_bbox` and `pages` are P1c bbox sums;
  - `flagged_suspect` = unique suspect vertices × cell;
  - `wrong_turn` = `wrong_turn_points` × cell;
  - `cleaned_kept` = cells kept in `cleaned/` × cell.

### A7.3 Axis: why the file is required
- Segment mode still requires an axis file (A5.3). Precisely, the axis fixes **only the sign of each crossing
  count**, for consistency with the trained features.
- SessA-2 shows detection, coverage, every |count| and every exclusion reason identical pair by pair under the box
  centroid and under the scroll axis (arms A = A-ax, B = B-ax; Scroll 1 umbilicus identical).
- Crop-centre orientation stays forbidden, because it flips signs relative to the training features (item-36).

### A7.4 On-ridge tests (softens A6.1's finding; the calibration rule stands)
- **Face offset:**
  - SessE-5, on 71 control hits: median **+1.6 voxels (~13 µm) outward**, IQR −1.7 to +3.5, split halves 0.4 and 2.3.
  - SessA's ±15.82 µm on two meshes is **one sampling step with opposite signs**: quantised, not confirmation.
  - SessC-2's raw 055 offset: +1.0 voxel (+7.9 µm) outward, 58 % positive, near the centreline.
  - "Half a sheet thickness" is plausible, not established.
- **Point-to-peak on-ridge tests are retired project-wide** until a band-aware instrument exists. There have been

  - SessE-4's ±1-voxel ray gate;
  - SessA's mesh-on-ridge reading;
- Any future band-aware instrument must still calibrate a per-product offset on control data (A6.1's rule).

### A7.5 Known limitation of the contract index: a fixed 134 µm spacing
- §2's Q3c solve uses `SP_UM = 134.0` (`phase/q3/q3_common.py` L25). This is the spacing the INDEX errata withdrew as

  SP_UM`, L82). Measurement (i) is a CT crossing count.

## Amendment 8 (2026-09-27). Adds to §4

### A8.1 Segment mode carries a power statement (SessA-4c)
- **Why.** The segment-mode decision rule (DBSCAN on flagged-pair midpoints, `eps` 200 µm, `min_samples` 5) cannot
  be met at deployment density.
  - At 400 pairs/cm², the most testable midpoints within 200 µm of any testable midpoint is **4** (Scroll 4 crop)
    and **3** (Scroll 1 crop).
  - A planted jump adds 0.15 flagged pairs to its box on average (SessA-3).
  - Zero clusters is therefore a threshold artefact, not evidence of absence.
- **Rule.** Every segment-mode `report.json` carries a `power` block:
  `{"decision_rule": str, "pairs_per_cm2": float, "testable_share": float, "testable_neighbours_within_eps":
  {"mean": float, "max": int}, "power": float | null, "power_method": str | null, "label": str}`.
  - `power` is the estimated probability that a jump of the reference size in the checked area produces a flag under
    this rule at this run's density. It is estimated by the method SessA-4 validates.
  - **If `power` < 0.5 or is null, `label` = "not a clean-segment test"**, and viewers show that label.
  - Until SessA-4 ships a validated method, `power` is null with a reason, and every segment run carries that label.
- Segment-mode clusters are not reported as detections, and zero clusters is not reported as "clean", until the
  rule is re-derived (SessA-4).
- Region mode is unaffected: its clusters are §4.1 clusters of switch-score flags, valid on the fixture (51,
  matching fixture v1.3).

### A8.2 Sampling density is per cm² only (SessA-4d)
- Pairs are drawn at a fixed density per cm² of checked mesh area. **No per-mesh minimum pair count.** SessA's
  500-pair floor raised the density above 400/cm² on meshes smaller than 1.25 cm², so the rule's behaviour depended
  on mesh size.
- `report.json` states `pairs_per_cm2` and the checked area in cm².

## Amendment 9 (2026-09-27). Adds to §4

### A9.1 What each mode ships
- **Region mode is the product** (patch pipelines, and the pipeline9 filter). Its outputs are §4's clusters,
  overlay, cleaned tifxyz and spiral constraints. This phase it still runs only on a committed wrap-index file
  (A5.6, A7.7).
- **Segment mode ships per-pair flags with a power statement**, not a verdict on a segment.
  - Dense sampling is the default: every vertex pair 100–400 µm apart along mesh edges (SessA-4 (a)).
  - The `power` block (A8.1) is required. The label "not a clean-segment test" applies whenever `power` < 0.5.
  - Every segment-mode `report.json` and README states the crossing count's two blind spots:
    - **contact** (sheets under ~25 µm apart): the count cannot separate touching sheets;
    - **gap**: a pair whose straight path crosses the inter-wrap gap leaves the field's support and is reported
      **untestable, not flagged**. A jump that runs through the gap is therefore invisible to the count.
  - No README, report or viewer text describes the tool as a general segment checker.

### A9.2 Crossing counts must be batch-independent
- A pair's count must depend only on that pair. The frozen `phase/x2/common.py` `Field.count` samples each 4,000-pair
  chunk at the chunk's longest sample count, so it does not meet this.
- Conforming implementations call `Field.count` once per group of pairs sharing a per-pair sample count
  (SessA-4's `check.count_dense`, `<branch>` da5da56), or an equivalent that is per-pair deterministic.
- The frozen file is not edited. Numbers computed with the batch-dependent call are marked as such (ledger item-63).

## Amendment 10 (2026-09-27). Amends A4.1 and A5.1

### A10.1 Why the overlay is full-frame (corrects A4.1's "Why" and A5.1's findings)
- **What A4.1 said was wrong.** It said VC3D "silently draws nothing" for a non-zero translation, citing the throw at
  `ZarrChunkFetcher.cpp:757` (755 by A5.1). SessD-1 read it that way, and integrator copied it.
- **What happens** (villa f4570bf, `volume-cartographer/core/src/render/ZarrChunkFetcher.cpp`, read by integrator):
  - A **local** open (`openLocalZarrPyramid`, 976–1008) takes only each dataset's `path` from `.zattrs`
    (`remoteLevelKeysFromZattrs`, 829). It never reads `coordinateTransformations`, so it **ignores the translation
    silently and draws the array at voxel − origin**.
  - The throw at **755** is in `strictRemoteLevelsFromZattrs`. Its only caller is `openHttpZarrPyramid`, and only for
    a rebased open (`strictRebasedOpen`, 1033–1036). So the rejection applies only to rebased HTTP opens.
  - SessD-2 measured the misplacement in-app: a region-form overlay drew exactly at voxel − origin (40/40,
    `evidence/vp2/probe_region.json`).
- **The decision stands:** full frame, translation 0, placement carried by array position and never by metadata.
  VC3D reads Zarr v2 and v3 (`utils/src/zarr.cpp:1360–1366`, SessD-2). The contract keeps v2.

### A10.2 The overlay region
- **Rule.** The overlay region is the bbox of:
  - every evaluated point (PA, PB and midpoint) of **every scored pair**, flagged or not; and
  - **every vertex the wrong-turn test evaluated.** This part is integrator's addition; see below.
- Add the 380 µm halo (A7.1), snap outward to the 128 grid, and clip to the scan. Helper:
  `contract_io.overlay_region`.
- Chunks are written only inside it, as in A4.1.
- **`report.json` gains `overlay_region`** `{origin_zyx, shape_zyx, halo_um, rule}`. `region` keeps its meaning: the
  analysis region (region mode) or the segment bbox plus halo (segment mode).
- **Validator** (`test_fixture.py --outputs`):
  - every cluster centre lies inside `overlay_region`;
  - every cluster's bbox holds at least one voxel of its overlay value (1 suspect join, 2 wrong turn);
  - a region-A run reproduces golden v1.4's `overlay_region`;
  - `--pre-a10` reports these checks as PENDING instead of failing, for a branch merged before it adopts A10.2.
- **Why the wrong-turn part.** A region from the scored pairs' points alone is not enough. On the fixture, it still
  leaves wrong-turn cluster 40 (centre z 5035) outside, because wrong-turn clusters are built from patch vertices,
  not from pair points. Using every *tested* vertex, not only the flagged ones, keeps the region independent of the
  results, as the pair part already is.
- **Region A** (fixture v1.4): the overlay region is origin (3712, 2176, 384) and shape (1408, 896, 1152). The
  analysis crop is 384³. Pair points alone give (3968, 2304, 384) and (1024, 768, 1024).

### A10.3 Missing chunks
- **VC3D** treats a chunk file that does not exist as "no sample", not as `fill_value`
  (`ChunkFetchStatus::Missing` at `ZarrChunkFetcher.cpp:288–291`; `ChunkedPlaneSampler.cpp:314–317` then returns no
  value).
  Under the overlay window [0.5, 2] this renders like 0, so omitting all-zero chunks is safe **for VC3D**.
- **Every other reader must apply `fill_value` (0)** to a missing chunk, as Zarr specifies. Missing does not mean
  "not computed". Outside `overlay_region` nothing was computed. Inside it, a missing chunk means 0.

## Amendment 11 (2026-09-27). Amends A2 and A3.2

### A11.1 Which files A3.2 ships (corrects A3.2's file list)
- **A3.2 listed the wrong files.** The decision there (uncut, uniform, per-patch `wind_a`, no filter variant) stands.
  - The two files it cites (141,449 + 4,808 point pairs, sha256 `0009f911…` / `100f8db9…`) are SessE-3's **filtered**
    file: the risk-v1 suspect-join cut plus SessE-1's abstention.
  - integrator took them from `sc3_ab_points.json` `k_q3c.export` without checking which variant that key held.
  - SessE-8b reconciles the two sets exactly (`sc8/reconcile_counts.py`, rerun by integrator: identical output).
- **The uncut set** is all **161,842** X6 evaluated point pairs: 146,320 same-winding + 15,522 relative-winding.
  SessE-3's 0.763 per-point hard accuracy (`post_hoc_baselines.k_q3c.acc_no_cut`) is on this set.
  - SessE-8b pins it after the anchor snap as `b863fe7e…4e6c` (same) and `835e9445…88f8c1` (relative), built by
    `sc8/ship_arm_a.sh`.
  - **Those files fail the full name check (A11.2).** SessE-8c's filtered files replace them, with the hashes pinned on
    `<branch>`.

### A11.2 Constraints must name patches villa actually loads (general rule for §A2)
- **Finding.** villa silently reassigns any constraint point whose named patch it did not load. It falls back to
  nearest-patch linking, with no error or warning.
  - At load villa trims one cell (4 voxels) off every patch edge (`erode_patch_valid_region`). It keeps a patch only
    if some valid cell survives inside the fit's z range.
  - In slab 2 (z 4096–4864), **50 of 6,704 patches** never load.
  - SessB's full check at villa f4570bf found 1,641 of 323,684 arm (a) points (0.51%) attached to a patch other than
    their own. 1,622 of them came through those 50 patches. The other 19 are same-winding ties between two loaded
    patches.
- **Rule. Before writing, the exporter applies villa's own load criterion at the villa commit the fit will run.**
  - A collection naming a patch that villa will not load is dropped.
  - Drops are counted per role and reported with the files.
  - Anchors lie on their own patch's trimmed surface (SessE-8 snap, item-71).
- **The name check covers every collection of every arm**, at the fit's villa commit, before any fit. A sample is not
  a pass. SessE-8's 150 + 150 smoke passed, yet the full check failed. SessE-8's own smoke output had already reported the
  50 patches as dropped.
- **Partner cases.** Points attached to the other named patch while both patches load (SessB's 19 "partner ties")
  are decided before a launch (drop or accept). The decision is recorded with the pinned hashes.

## Amendment 12 (2026-09-27). Amends A4.2 and A5.3

### A12.1 Segment-mode axis file: either format (R9)
- `--axis-file` accepts **our CSV** (`z,y,x` header, level-0 voxels; `phase/tools/axis/*.csv`) **or villa's
  `umbilicus.json`** (`{"control_points": [{"z", "y", "x"}]}`, level-0 voxels). SessE-8 wrote the latter for the slab
  (`phase/sc/vm/umbilicus.json`).
- **Reader:** `contract_io.read_axis_file`. A `coordinate_scale` other than 1.0 is refused. `axis_yx_at` interpolates
  linearly and returns the count of queries outside the control points' z range.
  - Ours clamps there; villa extrapolates linearly. So a run reports `axis_queries_outside` and never extrapolates
    silently.
- **Check:** `test_fixture.py` G6 reads both formats of the same axis identically. SessE-8's `umbilicus.json` read this
  way equals the committed CSV to 0.0 voxels over z 4096–4864 (integrator).
- **Plugin:** it looks for an umbilicus in the volume package. If there is none, segment mode is unavailable in the
  menu, with a one-line reason. Region mode is unaffected.

### A12.2 Region mode on the flat command line (replaces the need for SessD's adapter)
```
vc_sheet_check --region <patch dir> --wrap-index <file> --volume <ome-zarr root> --out <dir> [--threshold …]
vc_sheet_check --segment <tifxyz dir | .obj> --axis-file <csv | umbilicus.json> --volume <ome-zarr root> --out <dir> [--halo-um 380] [--threshold …]
```
- `--wrap-index` is required until SessA-6's solve lands. After that it becomes optional; leaving it out runs the solve.
- Exit codes, `status` and outputs are as in A4.2.

### A12.3 VC3D's level offset (R10): recorded, no contract change
- VC3D places level *l* voxel *a* at level-0 position 2^l·a. A 2× pyramid built over {2^l·a, …, 2^l·a + 2^l − 1} is
  therefore drawn offset by **−(2^l − 1)/2 level-0 voxels**. SessD-3 measured −0.5 at level 1.
- This applies to **every** volume VC3D shows, the scan included. It matters only if our overlay pyramid is
  downsampled differently from the scan's. SessD-5 checks the overlay-against-scan alignment at levels ≥ 1.
- The contract changes only if that check fails.

## Amendment 13 (2026-09-27). Amends A5.6, A7.7 and A12.2

### A13.1 The flat region form (replaces A12.2's region line)
```
vc_sheet_check --region Z Y X NZ NY NX --patches <tifxyz dir> --rel <rel.csv> --volume <ome-zarr root> --out <dir> [--wrap-index <file>] [--spacing-um N|estimate] [--threshold …]
```

- SessA-6's argument names are confirmed; they are no longer provisional. The segment line of A12.2 is unchanged.
- Exit codes, `status` and outputs are as in A4.2.

### A13.2 Region mode solves when `--wrap-index` is omitted (amends A5.6 and A7.7)
- Without `--wrap-index`, region mode runs the solve: SessA-6's port of the Q3c reference-free LP (§2). With it, the
  file is read as before. A7.7's "region mode is internal this phase" is withdrawn.
- `report.json` states the index source:
  - `wrap_index_source`: `"solve"` with the spacing used (µm) and whether it was estimated;
  - or `"file"` with the file's sha256.

### A13.3 Tiled regions share one support gate
- When a region's field is computed in tiles, the support gate is computed **once over the whole region** at
  level 1 and applied to every tile: Otsu threshold, filled envelope and amplitude floor τ. Per-tile adaptive gates
  are not allowed.
- **Why** (SessA-6, fixture A):
  - a per-tile gate halved testability, 28,356 testable points against 50,734 for one box;
  - with the shared gate, tiled and single-box fields give 55,212 and 55,348 testable points, equal counts on 99.6%
    of points testable in both, and **equal verdicts on 645 of 666 pairs**.
  - The 21 differing verdicts (3.2%) are the residual cost of tiling. The report states when a region was tiled.

## Amendment 14 (2026-09-27). Adds a rendering section (§7)

### A14.1 Flat-image renders (surface volumes, ink inputs, figures)
- **Layer rule** (SessI-4, measured on the control, `phase/ink/results/vmink4/render_check.json`):
  - layer k samples the CT at offset **k − 32 voxels along the inward normal**, with the normal set inward per pixel;
  - uint8 = uint16 / 257;
  - the ink model's window is layers 17..42.
- **Handedness.** For each pixel, h = sign((∂P/∂col × ∂P/∂row) · n_in), where:
  - P is the pixel's 3D scan position **in (z, y, x) component order**; the order matters, since writing P as
    (x, y, z) flips the sign;
  - col and row are the flat image's axes (x right, y down);
  - n_in is the inward normal.
- **The contract sign is h = +1** (the ink model's training convention). An image with h = −1 is mirror-imaged;
  flip its columns before inference or display.
- **Every render manifest carries** `handedness` (+1 or −1, the per-patch majority), `handedness_rule`
  ("CONTRACT A14.1"), the minority fraction, and the layer rule's parameters (offset origin 32, inward normal,
  divisor 257).
  - A render whose images mix signs is invalid until split.
  - Patches under 1,000 pixels may be excluded, and are counted.
- Why: SessC-3a's flattened q3/q4 grids were h = −1 on every measured patch (153), so SessI-4's images were mirrored. The
  model is not mirror-invariant: r 0.770 between mirrored and normal predictions on the control.

### A15.2 Axis rule (amends §2 for region mode; SessA-7 Amendment 2 plus SessA-8's scan keying)
- Region mode **never derives the axis from the region's own patch centroids**. `--axis table` is refused (exit 2).

## Amendment 16 (2026-09-27). Amends A14.1

### A16.1 Handedness is measured per flattened component
- pipeline9's `fm` flattens each connected component **in its own frame**. A component's flattened handedness follows
  its **root patch's own grid**, the first patch in `patchorders.csv` (SessC-6: 18 of 18, found post hoc). So one set can
  mix signs: SessC-6 measured 10 of 18 components at −1 and 8 at +1.
- **Rule:** measure h (A14.1) **per flattened component** and flip each −1 component at the source.
- Each render manifest lists, per component:
  - `component`, `root_patch`, the measured `handedness` before any flip, and `flipped` (true/false);
  - `handedness_written` (must be +1) and the minority fraction.
- A render that records one sign for a whole multi-component set is invalid.

### A16.2 The flat-grid origin line is masked for inference
- pipeline9's flat grids lose one grid line per axis at flat coordinate 0 (SessC-6). The line holds about 1 point where
  its neighbours hold about 420, and it shows as a thin dark cross in every `f` / `fm` render.
- **Rule:** before any inference, fill those pixels by interpolation from their neighbours, and record the mask of
  filled pixels with the render. Record the mask's file and its pixel count in the manifest.
- Ink maps show masked pixels as masked, so a filled line never reads as ink or as its absence.

## Amendment 17 (2026-09-28). Amends §2 (solver)

### A17.1 Defect found and fixed: the solve's result depended on the LP solver under ties
- **Found by SessA (SessA-12b, 7fc2576).** The solve has two stages. Stage 1 solves the (i)+(ii) LP for kA. Stage 2 builds
  the Stevens targets from the signs of kA's differences and solves the final LP. Stage 1's optimum is **not
  unique** on slab 2: every method reaches the same optimal objective (1306), but different optimal vertices give
  different Stevens targets and so different final indices.

  | Solver (slab 2) | Final objective | Patches whose wrap index differs from the committed index |
  |---|---|---|
  | HiGHS simplex, default or dual | 2114 | 0 (byte-identical to the committed index) |
  | Min-cost circulation | 2116 | 144 |
  | HiGHS interior point | 2107 | 52 |

- **integrator reran all three** at `<branch>` bc6bd28 in the contract environment. The numbers are identical
  (`phase/writeup/int133_tie/v1_12b_bench_rerun.json`).
- So §2's "exact LP" did not define a unique index. Which index came out depended on HiGHS's vertex choice.

### A17.2 Rule: ties go toward the radial-gap estimate (as implemented by SessA-15, `<branch>` 95c9755 / f0becd0)
- **Every LP call whose solution is used minimises** `primary + ε · Σ_i |k_i − r_i|`, with **ε = 1 / (4M)**.
  - `primary` is §2's uniform-weight L1 objective. Its terms, weights and cut adjustment are unchanged.
  - `M` is the number of primary terms in that call.
- **r_i, the rounded radial-gap estimate:** `r_i = round((ρ_i − ρ_A) / SP_vox)`.
  - `ρ_i` is the distance of the patch centroid from the solve axis at its z.
  - `A` is the anchor (smallest node index) of the largest primary component.
  - `SP_vox` is the solve spacing / 7.91 µm.
  - There is no handedness factor (the d_ii targets carry none).
  - This supersedes integrator's first reading (unrounded ρ_i/Δ), which was written before SessA's request was read.
- **Gauge:** k is measured from a virtual anchor node v0 (k_v0 = 0), so the ε-edges place every component. §2's
  comparison rule is unchanged: compare only after one constant per component.
- **Which calls.** The rule applies to stage 1 (kA) **and to the final LP**, which settles whether stage 2 has
  ties. The primary-optimum check below holds on every call. The handedness choice uses only the two stage-1 optimal objectives, which are unique, so it is unaffected.
- **Implementation:** the dual min-cost circulation (OR-Tools `SimpleMinCostFlow`), with primary weights × 4M and one
  weight-1 edge v0 → i (target r_i) per patch. That is exactly ε = 1/(4M), in integers. k is recovered as potentials.
- **Checks on every call, recorded in `wrap_index.json`:**
  1. primal = dual;
  2. the primary objective equals the plain (untied) optimum for the same terms.
- **Why the rule cannot move the primary optimum (integrator).** With uniform integer weights, the primary is a sum of convex
  functions of integer differences. So any integer k that is not primary-optimal has a move of ±1 on some set S of
  patches that lowers the primary by at least 1, while changing the tie term by at most `ε · |S| ≤ n / (4M)`. That is
  below 1 whenever M ≥ n/4, which holds for any connected term graph (M ≥ n − 1). Check 2 verifies it on every run.
- **Still open (integrator):** a residual-tie check. Re-solve with ε/2 and require the identical k, or report where it
  differs.
- **Unchanged:** the Stevens target convention (`raw == 0 → +1`, `build_terms_reffree`), itself a fixed tie rule.
- **Known bias (open).** On the whole scroll the tie term is large: Σ abs(k − r) ≈ 579k, about 10 wraps
  per patch, and the largest component's anchor lands at k = 7. So r drifts from the solved k where the pitch is not
  134 µm. It cannot move the primary optimum (ε · 579k ≈ 0.43 < 1, checked), but ties are broken toward a biased
  estimate. A local pitch per z band would make r a better tie-breaker; that is a later refinement.

### A17.3 The reference solve for new work
- **The exact min-cost circulation with A17.2 is the reference solve for all new work.** Any other solver path is
  allowed only if it reproduces that solve's `wrap_index.csv` byte-identically.
- SessA's fast path (bc6bd28: HiGHS dual simplex for kA and the final LP) reproduces the **committed** index. From now on
  it is a legacy-reproduction path, not the contract solve.

### A17.4 Existing rows keep the committed index
- The committed slab-2 index (`phase/p1page/p1b_q3c_k.csv`) and every row, golden file and baseline hash built on it
  stay unchanged.
- It is annotated **"HiGHS tie choice; differs from the contract solve on 20 patches"**. N = 20 of 6,704 is counted
  after one constant per component (§2 Gauge). SessA-15 reported it, and integrator recomputed the tie-broken slab-2 index at
  `<branch>` b696724: it is identical to SessA's `results/v1-15/slab2/wrap_index_tiebroken.csv`, with N = 20.
  - The contract solve's final objective on slab 2 is **2107**, below the committed path's 2114.
  - SessA reports that none of the 20 is in SessE's 936-patch block.
- **The fixture golden files stay on the committed index** (SessA's request; the working rule keeps shared fixtures and
  baseline hashes unchanged). SessA reproduces them with `tiebreak=False` / `--no-tiebreak`. A tie-broken fixture, if
  wanted, is a separately recorded version.
